memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So God said to Noah, "I am going to put an end to all people, for the earth is filled with violence because of them. So make yourself an ark of cypress wood; make rooms in it and coat it with pitch inside and out." - Gen 6:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God shares His plan with Noah - both the judgement that is coming and the way of rescue. Judgement is real: "I am going to put an end to all people." But in the same breath, God provides a way of salvation: "make yourself an ark." The very God who announces the flood also provides the boat. Judgement and mercy come together.

This is the pattern of the whole Bible. God never leaves the world without a way of rescue. Before the waters ever rose, God gave Noah the plans for salvation. The ark was entirely God's idea, God's design, God's provision. Noah could never have thought of it or saved himself; he simply had to receive and obey what God provided.

The ark points beautifully to Christ. Just as there was only one ark, one door, one way through the flood, so there is one Saviour who carries us safely through the judgement we deserve. "Salvation is found in no one else" (Acts 4:12). To be "in the ark" was to be safe; to be "in Christ" is to be saved.

The wonderful truth is that God is not a God who only judges. He is a God who, alongside every warning of judgement, provides a way of escape for all who will trust Him. Have you entered the ark of His salvation?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you see that God provides rescue alongside judgement?
- Have you taken refuge in Christ, the ark of salvation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Saving God, thank You that You provide rescue for those who trust You. Thank You for Jesus, my ark and my refuge. Keep me safe in Him through every storm.
